title: Delirium and Agitation Near End of Life

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults near the end of life with anxiety, delirium or agitation: identifying reversible causes, non-drug care, and benzodiazepine or antipsychotic trials. Verified against NICE NG31 and Saudi MOH Protocol-010 (steroid adverse effects); doses from US FDA labels where NICE gives none.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Doses from FDA labels for other indications (off-label in delirium)
SC dosing and midazolam — local formulary

pathophysiology.summary: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and cognition caused by physical illness or drugs. Near the end of life it is common and often multifactorial; agitation alone may reflect unrelieved pain or bodily needs (NICE NG31).
keyMechanisms: Brain dysfunction from metabolic failure (renal failure, hyponatraemia, hypercalcaemia), infection, hypoxia or drugs.
Drugs: opioids, benzodiazepines, anticholinergics (including atropine and hyoscine hydrobromide for secretions), corticosteroids (MOH lists delirium and psychosis).
Unrelieved pain, full bladder or rectum can present as agitation (NICE NG31 1.5.23).
In the last days delirium may be irreversible; goals shift to comfort and safety.

symptoms: Fluctuating confusion, inattention, disorientation; hyperactive (restless, distressed) or hypoactive (withdrawn, drowsy).
physicalSigns: Restlessness, picking at bedclothes, myoclonus (opioid toxicity).
Palpable bladder, faecal loading, pain behaviours.
redFlags: No response to antipsychotic — specialist advice (NICE NG31 1.5.28)
Uncertain diagnosis of delirium versus other distress

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Palpable bladder or rectal loading; settles once relieved.
Myoclonus, pinpoint pupils, drowsiness after dose increase.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Distinguish delirium from anxiety; explore causes with family (NICE NG31 1.5.23).

clinicalManagement.title: Look for causes
actions: Check pain, bladder, bowels, drugs, infection, hypoxia and metabolic causes (NICE NG31 1.5.23–1.5.25).
Treat reversible causes when consistent with the person's goals.

clinicalManagement.title: Non-drug care
actions: Calm, familiar environment; family presence; reorientation; avoid restraint (NICE NG31 1.5.24).

clinicalManagement.title: Drug trial
actions: Anxiety or agitation: trial of a benzodiazepine (NICE NG31 1.5.26) — e.g. lorazepam 2–3 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses (elderly or debilitated 1–2 mg/day) per FDA label.
Delirium or agitation: trial of an antipsychotic (NICE NG31 1.5.27) — e.g. haloperidol 0.5–2 mg two to three times daily (FDA label initial range).
Start at the low end in frail patients; review response and sedation at least daily.

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate
actions: Seek specialist palliative care advice if diagnosis is uncertain, no response to antipsychotic, or unwanted sedation (NICE NG31 1.5.28).

learningObjectives: Identify reversible causes of end-of-life delirium and agitation and use cautious drug trials.

keyPoints: Agitation may be pain or a full bladder.
Benzodiazepine for anxiety; antipsychotic for delirium.
pitfalls: Sedating before checking bladder and bowels.

patientEducation: Explain delirium to family; it is a medical complication, not a personality change.
Family presence and familiar objects help.
lifestyleAndDiet: Quiet, well-lit environment; sleep routine; reorientation.
dischargeCriteria: Symptoms controlled for the chosen place of care, or safe transfer arranged.
Patient and family know the plan, the medicines and whom to call.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review at least daily and after each dose change; involve family in monitoring.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Acute fluctuating inattention and altered cognition
Uncertain diagnosis, no response to antipsychotic, or unwanted sedation

regimens.indication: Delirium or agitation near end of life (antipsychotic trial)
adjustments: Label initial range for moderate symptoms (psychosis); use in delirium is off-label (NICE NG31 gives no dose)

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG31 recommends benzodiazepine and antipsychotic trials without doses; the doses shown are FDA-label initial ranges (haloperidol for psychotic symptoms, lorazepam for anxiety) and are off-label for end-of-life delirium. SC routes and midazolam per local palliative formulary. Check SFDA registration.
